name: MQTT.js
solves: Provides a full-featured MQTT client for Node.js and browsers to publish and subscribe over MQTT 3.1/5.0 — the standard for IoT and broker-based telemetry, not a general-purpose web multiplayer or chat transport.
best_for: IoT and device fleets that speak MQTT to brokers (Mosquitto, HiveMQ, AWS IoT Core)
Telemetry and event buses that use topic hierarchies with QoS and retained messages
Node or browser clients that must interoperate with existing MQTT infrastructure
Bridging devices to cloud IoT platforms via MQTT.js
Industrial or embedded systems where MQTT is already the organizational standard
skip_when: You are building browser collaborative docs, multiplayer presence, or chat — use Yjs, Liveblocks, Socket.IO, Ably, or Pusher instead
You need a managed WebSocket pub/sub UX for consumer web apps
You only need raw WebSockets without MQTT protocol semantics — use `ws`
Your environment blocks MQTT ports and you lack a WebSocket MQTT bridge
Application-level rooms and namespaces (Socket.IO) fit better than MQTT topic hierarchies

hosted_alternative.name: Ably
hosted_alternative.pricing_summary: Free tier with message limits; paid plans scale with messages and connections — better default for web app realtime than self-running MQTT
